newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African strike bites for second day in a row.
newsitem.headline: S.African strike bites for second day in a row.

text.p: South African workers widely supported a second day of strike action on Tuesday to press demands for improved employment conditions in a new law.
Cosatu, the 1.9 million-member Congress of South African Trade Unions, has called four days of regional strikes ending on Thursday urging a 40-hour work week and six months maternity leave.
Employers reported a strong response in the east coast province of KwaZulu-Natal on Tuesday after the first 24-hour strike hit hard in the automobile-producing province of the Eastern Cape.
Durban Harbour -- the busiest port in Africa -- was affected by the stayaway with no breakbulk cargo being handled, a Portnet spokeswoman said.
"The container services are 67 percent operational. Road transport services have been affected, but I don't have figures," Portnet spokeswoman Yvonne de Kock told Reuters, without elaborating.
Police said an incident of intimidation was reported near the black township of Umlazi near Durban where a bus carrying workers was stoned. No injuries were reported.

The disputed Basic Conditions of Employment Bill is due to go to parliament on September 15. Employers' groups argue that some of the bill's provisions could raise employment costs, already higher than many competitors', deterring job creation.

Labour Minister Tito Mboweni, increasingly concerned that his ministry will not be able to present the bill in parliament this year, has warned that delays might result in the proposed law "withering away" -- a fate the unions are anxious to avoid.
